active_paradigms.idea: Replace stochastic basin hopping with a symmetry-reduced global search using scipy.optimize.differential_evolution
active_paradigms.description: The current program first performs spherical inverse-power repulsion, then applies many SLSQP solves to the full 39-coordinate constrained problem. Its strength is the correct diameter-one formulation with analytic derivatives, which reaches the apparent reference contact graph; its principal weakness is that SLSQP is local and the many random perturbations mostly revisit the same basin. Instead, encode a plausible high-symmetry 14-point orbit construction with only a few geometric parameters, such as ring radii, heights, angular offsets, and any distinct orbit representatives under a chosen finite rotation/reflection group. Evaluate the true squared ratio directly after centering and scaling by the candidate diameter, so no separate scale variable or upper-distance constraints are needed. Call scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once on the bounded reduced parameter vector, with a fixed seed, Sobol initialization, polishing enabled, and tight tolerances. The optimizer should search several symmetry classes in separate program variants, rather than treating a single full-coordinate local optimum as evidence that its contact graph is globally best. This is especially promising because the score is already within numerical noise of the benchmark, so identifying the exact symmetry family can remove small asymmetries and expose a better contact configuration.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The sole target is the evaluator's squared ratio (minimum pairwise squared distance divided by maximum pairwise squared distance). Reducing dimension makes global topology/contact-graph changes more likely than the current perturb-and-SLSQP schedule.
active_paradigms.cautions: The construction must always emit exactly 14 finite points; avoid parameterizations that merge orbit points at zero radius. The objective is nonsmooth when the identity of a shortest or diameter pair changes, so use a sufficiently large population and do not infer success from a smoothed surrogate alone. A symmetry restriction can miss an asymmetric optimum, so use several independently motivated orbit parameterizations as alternative submitted programs, not sequential optimizations in one call.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a contact-graph equation solve with scipy.optimize.least_squares to obtain an exact rigid candidate
active_paradigms.description: The current code already reveals the useful principle: after diameter normalization, the optimum is governed by a small set of active lower-distance contacts and active diameter pairs, while most of its 182 inequalities are slack. Its weakness is that SLSQP repeatedly handles all inequalities and can terminate with small residual violations or an imprecise, slightly asymmetric realization of the same active graph. Build a fixed candidate contact graph from the near-reference configuration: include pairs repeatedly attaining the minimum distance, pairs attaining the diameter, and enough additional contacts to make the framework rigid after fixing translation, rotation, and scale. Parameterize the 14 coordinates in a gauge-fixed form and use scipy.optimize.least_squares once to solve residual equations d_ij^2-u=0 for short contacts and d_ij^2-1=0 for diameter contacts, with optional residuals enforcing intended symmetry. Start from a fixed, hard-coded numerical approximation of the known candidate rather than conducting a preceding optimizer run. After the solve, return the coordinates directly and let the evaluator compute the actual extrema; inactive pairs then certify whether this contact graph is feasible and superior. This attacks numerical error and contact degeneracy rather than merely launching more random full-dimensional searches.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exact equalization of the distance classes that determine dmin and dmax, thereby improving the true squared ratio and reducing loss from SLSQP feasibility tolerances.
active_paradigms.cautions: least_squares is an equation solver, not a global maximizer: the selected graph must be independently feasible and rigid, and every noncontact pair must be checked after solving. Fix a complete Euclidean gauge, for example point 0 at the origin, point 1 on the x-axis, point 2 in the xy-plane, plus one diameter normalization, or the Jacobian will be rank deficient. Do not force all near-short pairs to equality if the intended optimum requires some of them to be slack.

active_paradigms.idea: Directly optimize the normalized max-min objective with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing in gauge-fixed coordinates
active_paradigms.description: The existing implementation is a hybrid of spherical-code seeding, constrained local SQP, and many incumbent perturbations. This works because spherical repulsion provides well-separated points and analytic constraints make local polishing efficient, but it is biased toward spherical seeds and has no mechanism for accepting a temporary score decrease needed to change the nearest-neighbor graph. Use a gauge-fixed coordinate vector for 14 unrestricted 3D points, with translation removed and a fixed overall box large enough to contain a diameter-one realization. Define one scale-invariant objective as the negative of min(d2)/max(d2), computed from all 91 squared distances, and add deterministic tiny tie-breaking only if needed for numerical stability. Make exactly one scipy.optimize.dual_annealing call with a fixed seed, broad but justified coordinate bounds, high visit parameter, and a local search option using its built-in polishing facility. Unlike the constrained formulation, this has no feasibility boundary: every noncoincident configuration has a valid score, and annealing can cross changes in which pair realizes the diameter or minimum. A successful result can reveal a distinct contact topology; it is then also a source of a fixed candidate for a later equation-based construction, though that later step should be in a separate program variant.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global improvement of the actual evaluator quantity, including moves that alter both the minimum-distance contact graph and the diameter graph simultaneously.
active_paradigms.cautions: The ratio is undefined at collapsed configurations, so return a large finite penalty whenever max(d2) is tiny or any value is nonfinite. Bounds should only fix gauge and numerical scale; they must not impose an artificial unit-cube geometric restriction. Full 36-dimensional annealing may be costly, so combine it with a fixed symmetry-aware or gauge-reduced parameterization when timeout is tight, and always use a fixed random seed.
